newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan denies crown prince to meet Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Jordan denies crown prince to meet Netanyahu.

text.p: Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan will not attend a ceremony at the Israeli-Jordan border on Tuesday in memory of seven Israeli girls killed by a Jordanian soldier, a Jordanian palace official said on Monday.

Earlier Israel's Government Press Office said Crown Prince Hassan and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu would hold diplomatic talks and speak at a memorial ceremony before Netanyahu visited the "Island of Peace", a border area where the seven schoolgirls were shot dead on March 13.
"We never said the crown prince will be going, he is not going," the palace official told Reuters.
The official said a ceremony would be held in the area known in Jordan as Baqoura attended by lower level Jordanian officials.
The girls' parents are to dedicate a "hill of flowers" and plant trees at the site on Tuesday, the Israeli press office said in a statement.

Jordan's King Hussein paid a condolence call on the victims' families after the attack and expressed shame at the massacre which took place at a beauty spot on Jordanian soil leased to Israeli farmers under a 1994 peace deal.

Netanyahu media adviser David Bar-Illan told Israel Radio the issues to be discussed at the meeting included the building of a joint airport on the Red Sea, diverting Jordan River water to Jordan, tourism projects at the Dead Sea and other industry and trade issues.

"There are various ideas - some of them have been realised, some are in the process of planning and some are almost implemented," Bar-Illan said. "All this should and can be accelerated we believe, and I'm sure this meeting will do something in that direction."
New Israeli ambassador to Amman, Oded Eran, told the radio there was disenchantment in Jordan over the three-year-old peace accord with Israel, and expectations of "more tangible" economic results.
